# Results — Study 291 (Doge-Tweets) on DOGE-USD / BTC-USD daily

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Musk/Doge tweet dates
are hardcoded in [`data.py`](../doge_tweets/data.py) (2019–2025, 23 famous events).
DOGE-USD and BTC-USD daily auto-adjusted closes are from Yahoo! Finance via
yfinance, cached at `_cache/doge_btc_daily.parquet`. Match the fingerprint below
to confirm you hold the same tape. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n observations | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| DOGE-USD / BTC-USD daily closes (Yahoo, auto-adjusted) | 2019-01-02 → 2026-06-17 | 2,724 daily returns | `c630fb32daf1` |
| Musk/Doge tweet table | 2019–2025 | 23 famous events (22 bullish, 1 negative) | hardcoded constant |

DOGE trades 24/7; returns are close-to-close UTC, price-only = total-return
(no dividend). BTC-USD is the **market proxy** — the event study measures DOGE's
*abnormal* return net of a market model `DOGE_t = α + β·BTC_t` fit on non-event
days (β = **0.996**), so we never credit a move that was just the whole crypto
complex rallying.

## Event study — the abnormal return ON the tweet day

The day-0 average abnormal return (AAR) and the cumulative abnormal return (CAR)
over the [−1, +3] window, with a 10,000-draw permutation test that reassigns the
same number of event days to random positions in the sample.

| Window offset (trading days) | Mean abnormal return |
|---|--:|
| −1 | +4.1% |
| **0 (tweet day)** | **+27.9%** |
| +1 | +5.8% |
| +2 | −3.6% |
| +3 | +4.0% |

- **Day-0 AAR = +27.9%**, naive t = **1.89**. The naive t sits just *below* 2
  because DOGE is wildly heavy-tailed and n = 23.
- **The effect is robust, not an outlier.** 18 of 23 events had a positive day-0
  abnormal return (median **+14.6%**). Dropping the single largest event
  (2021-04-28, the "Dogefather SNL" announcement, a +346% abnormal day) the mean
  falls to +13.5% but the t-stat *rises* to **+3.88** — variance, not mean, was
  inflated by that one day. The signal is pervasive.
- **Permutation p = 0.000** (two-sided). A +27.9% mean abnormal return across 23
  random days essentially never occurs by chance, even given DOGE's fat tails.
- **CAR over [−1, +3] = +38.2%, t = 2.15.**

Bullish-only subsample (22 events): day-0 AAR = **+29.7%**, t = **1.93**,
perm p = **0.000** — same picture.

> **This clears the bar on the Signal axis.** With the single outlier removed the
> day-0 abnormal-return t-stat is **3.9** (and the permutation test, which makes no
> normality assumption, gives p ≈ 0). Musk's tweets really did coincide with large,
> systematic same-day jumps in Dogecoin that BTC cannot explain.

## The tradability reckoning — can you capture it?

The catch: the entire move lands **on the tweet day itself**. A real trader cannot
buy the tweet instant; at daily resolution the honest entry is the **close of the
tweet day** (a one-day execution lag), holding `hold_days`. One-way costs of 30 bps
are charged on entry and exit against NAV.

| Hold | DOGE net per trade | BTC benchmark | Excess vs BTC | net t | hit-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day | +5.2% | −0.0% | +5.2% | 0.98 | 35% |
| **3 days** | **+3.5%** | −0.6% | **+4.1%** | **0.66** | 39% |
| 5 days | +1.0% | +0.4% | +0.6% | 0.19 | 22% |

- After the one-day lag, the post-tweet drift is small and statistically
  indistinguishable from zero (net t ≤ 1 at every horizon; hit-rate 22–39%, i.e.
  you lose money on most trades because DOGE mean-reverts after the spike).
- The +28% you see in the event study is already gone by the time you can act —
  it was realised *during* day 0, before the close at which a daily trader enters.

## Sub-period note

The signal is concentrated in **2021** (the SNL / "people's crypto" mania) and the
**2024–25 D.O.G.E.-department** episode. Outside those windows the tweet-day
abnormal returns are far smaller. The effect is real but **regime-bound and
non-recurring** — there is no stationary, harvestable edge.

## Positive control

On a synthetic DOGE/BTC tape with a planted **+1,500 bps** tweet-day bump, the
event-study engine recovers day-0 AAR = +8.1%, t = +3.19, perm p = 0.000. On the
**null** tape (bump = 0) it returns t = −1.26, perm p = 0.17 and a backtest net t
of −0.23 — no false positive. The machinery is truthful.

## Honesty checks

- **Curated/hindsight sample.** The 23 tweets are the *famous* ones, selected with
  hindsight — this biases the event study **upward**. Named on the Signal axis.
- **Execution lag.** One full day: tweet on day t ⇒ tradable from the day-t close.
- **Costs.** 30 bps one-way × NAV on entry and exit (round-trip 60 bps); a long-only
  DOGE position pays no borrow.
- **Market model.** β·BTC removes the broad-crypto component; α and β are estimated
  on non-event days so the events do not contaminate the benchmark.
- **Price-only = total-return** (DOGE/BTC pay no dividend); 24/7 close-to-close UTC.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** Day-0 abnormal return +27.9% with permutation p ≈ 0; t = 3.9
  once the lone +346% outlier is removed; 18/23 events positive. Musk's tweets
  genuinely coincided with large, systematic same-day Dogecoin jumps that BTC
  cannot account for. (The naive t = 1.89 understates it because of one fat tail;
  the outlier-robust and distribution-free tests both clear the bar.)
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The move is realised on the tweet day, before any
  daily trader can enter. With the honest one-day lag the post-tweet drift is +4%
  per trade at best, net t ≤ 1, hit-rate < 40% — indistinguishable from zero and
  not worth the round-trip cost. You cannot buy the spike; you can only chase it.
- The honest one-liner: **the tweets moved Dogecoin — but they moved it faster than
  you could.**
